title: sales-cs-inbound-ask-merging-lens-and-implementation-fitness-score
creator: Liam O'Connell
description: Problem: Sales and CS submit many high-touch feature asks that overlap or compete for the same platform investments. Current intake creates duplicate efforts and inconsistent scoping. Goal: Build a repeatable 'Ask Merging Lens' that automatically groups related inbound enterprise asks and attaches an 'Implementation Fitness Score' to each group to enable fast prioritization and initial scoping. Scope: - Define grouping heuristics (semantic similarity, shared customer cohort, affected surface area) - Define Implementation Fitness Score formula (effort proxy + infra risk + customer ARR + synergies) - Produce a lightweight scoping sheet per group with recommended route: Quick-win, Partner pilot, Full implementation, or Decline - Deliver a small UI in the CS intake dashboard for PMs to accept/override merges Out of scope: full technical design/costs for individual feature builds; final roadmap decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Automated grouping reduces duplicate inbound items by >= 35% in an initial 30-day run
Each group is annotated with an Implementation Fitness Score and a recommended route (Quick-win/Partner pilot/Full/Decline)
PM/SE raters agree with automated grouping >= 70% in a blind validation sample of 50 groups
Prototype scoping sheet created for at least 3 top groups including estimated effort band (S/M/L) and one recommended next step
Integration point documented with CS intake dashboard and a Confluence playbook linked from the ticket
success_metrics: Time-to-first-validated-scope for enterprise asks reduced from median 7d to <= 3d
Fraction of inbound asks that are routed to an actionable next step increases by 25%
Reduction in duplicated engineering work identified during quarterly review by 30%
proposed_approach: Phase 1: Data exploration — run historical similarity clustering on past 18 months of CS+Sales asks and surface candidate merge groups (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Scoring design — define Implementation Fitness Score components and weights with Eng/Infra/Revenue input (1 week)
Phase 3: Lightweight prototype — automated grouping + score in a staging view of CS intake dashboard; PMs can edit merges and scores (3 weeks)
Phase 4: Validation & rollout — measure agreement metrics and iterate; publish Confluence playbook and CS training (2 weeks)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Over-aggregating distinct asks could hide customer-specific constraints — mitigated by surfacing example submissions and owner contact info
Score may bias towards high-ARR customers — ensure a fairness check and visibility into non-ARR signals (strategic value, regulatory needs)
Automation requires data hygiene (consistent tagging and summary quality) — initial manual review cadence needed
comments: 2026-03-03 - Liam O'Connell: Kickoff with CS and Sales reps. Priority set to P1 after examples surfaced from three accounts. Asked Eng to pull last 18 months of inbound asks for clustering.

2026-03-08 - Priya Nair (CS): Reviewed merges for strategic customers; recommended preserving account-level exceptions and adding an 'account veto' flag in the UI.
2026-03-09 - Design (Eleni Park): Shared intake UI sketches; suggested inline rationale and examples next to each proposed merge to aid reviewer trust.
